answer:
In the 17th century BCE (raw-anchor transition at the BCE 1800→1700 boundary; calendar-century window BCE 1700–1601), Diversity in Pottery Form collapses (ΔZKeform = −1.870 ≈ 1.89σ) while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases (ΔZkeverz = +1.450 ≈ 1.58σ) simultaneously — the largest such joint event in the BCE 4100–500 in-range span.

Sign convention footnote (mandatory): the time-series column `CE` uses `CE = −BCE` (verified by tying `time_series.PotteryForm` at CE to `capital.ZKeform` at the matching BCE across all 37 BCE anchors). Therefore the raw anchor year "BCE 1800" corresponds to CE −1800, BCE 1700 to CE −1700, and the 17th century BCE (calendar-century convention: N-th century BCE = BCE [N·100, (N−1)·100 + 1]) corresponds to the CE window [−1700, −1601].

Secondary caveat (not affecting the headline): at BCE 1100→1000 a smaller, decoration-only elevation occurs (ZKeform stays at its −1.13σ floor, Zkeverz rises +0.97→+1.53, Δdec = 0.56); this is a second-order decorative peak with no simultaneous form-collapse and is therefore explicitly excluded from the headline. The pre-history BCE 4300/4200 segment (flat plateau −1.13 / −1.92; outside the time_series coverage CE ∈ [−4100, −500]) is also excluded.

payload.hypothesis: In the 17th century BCE (raw-anchor transition at the BCE 1800→1700 boundary; calendar-century window BCE 1700–1601), Diversity in Pottery Form collapses (ΔZKeform = −1.870 ≈ 1.89σ_form) while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases (ΔZkeverz = +1.450 ≈ 1.58σ_dec) simultaneously — the largest such joint event in the BCE 4100–500 in-range span. Derived directly from capital.csv 100-year anchors (ZKeform, Zkeverz), confirmed on time_series_data.csv PotteryForm_inter/PotteryDecoration_inter, and robust at 0.3σ/0.5σ/1.0σ thresholds. Sign convention: CE = −BCE, so BCE 1800 ↔ CE −1800; N-th century BCE = BCE [N·100, (N−1)·100 + 1].
payload.workflow: 1) Align the two files on 100-year BCE bins using capital.csv as the canonical source of ZKeform (Pottery Form) and Zkeverz (Pottery Decoration); verify CE = −BCE by tying time_series.PotteryForm at CE to capital.ZKeform at BCE for all 37 in-range BCE anchors (BCE 4100..500). 2) Exclude the BCE 4300 and BCE 4200 rows in capital.csv because they sit outside the time_series_data.csv coverage (CE starts at −4100) and form a flat −1.13/−1.92 plateau with no transition signal. 3) Compute raw centennial Δ-step (d_ZKeform, d_Zkeverz) at every BCE anchor; jointly evaluate with multi-thresholds ≥0.3σ/≥0.5σ/≥1.0σ using σ_form=0.989 and σ_dec=0.917 from the in-range raw anchors. 4) Confirm with smoothed _inter series that PotteryForm_inter decreases monotonically and PotteryDecoration_inter increases monotonically across the BCE 1800→1700 boundary. 5) Calendar-century labelling convention: N-th century BCE = BCE [N·100, (N−1)·100 + 1]; report the event as '17th century BCE' (BCE 1700..1601 = CE −1700..−1601) following the researcher instruction. 6) Investigate the BCE 1100→1000 case and explicitly EXCLUDE it as a second-order decorative elevation only (ZKeform stays at the −1.13σ collapse floor; no simultaneous form collapse). 7) Rank simultaneous events by |Δform|+|Δdec|; the BCE 1800→1700 event yields joint score 3.32, the largest non-trivial simultaneous event.
payload.sign_convention_footnote: CE = −BCE consistently across both files. Example: cap.csv row '1800 LN ZKeform=+0.74 Zkeverz=−0.48' anchors the same instant as time_series.PotteryForm at CE = −1800 (= +0.74) and PotteryDecoration at CE = −1800 (= −0.48). Therefore 'BCE 1800' equals 'CE −1800', and the 17th century BCE (calendar-century convention N-th c. BCE = BCE [N·100, (N−1)·100 + 1]) corresponds to the CE window [−1700, −1601].
payload.secondary_event_caveat: BCE 1100->1000: ZKeform unchanged at -1.13σ floor, Zkeverz rises +0.97->+1.53 (Δdec ≈ +0.56). Decoration-only elevation, NOT a simultaneous collapse; explicitly excluded from the headline hypothesis.
payload.robustness_bands: raw Δ at BCE 1800->1700 boundary: form -1.870 (1.89σ_form), dec +1.450 (1.58σ_dec); passes all three thresholds (≥0.3σ, ≥0.5σ, ≥1.0σ) on both axes.
